reasons: Financial pressure 4 of 4 (going concern, covenant problem, incentive pay tied to revenue/EPS, capital raise all present): maximum pressure, giving a strong motive to manage reported results.

Internal control and audit 2 of 4: two flags among material weakness, adverse ICFR opinion, auditor change and disagreement point to weak controls and/or friction with the auditor, i.e. less chance of catching misstatements.
Prior-period corrections 1 of 3: a restatement/revision, voluntary accounting change or segment change was present, so either past errors or a change in accounting judgement.
Management turnover 1 of 2: a CEO/CFO change or an interim CFO, which under severe pressure raises control and transition risk.
Transaction complexity 3 of 8: several judgement-heavy areas (e.g. over-time revenue, contract assets, related parties, acquisitions, write-downs, concentration) give room to manipulate results.
Numeric warning signals 2 of 4 computable: two of Beneish M, Dechow F, high accruals and low OCF/net income are triggered, consistent with accrual-driven earnings.

No investigations or litigation flags (0 of 3) slightly reduce the score. The card has no specific F/R items, only area counts, so the assessment is coarse. Even so, flags cluster across pressure, controls, corrections and numeric areas.
